Rashi on Berakhot 33a:11:1.hebrew: מזכירין גבורות גשמים - משיב הרוח, שאינו לשון בקשה אלא לשון הזכרה ושבח:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:11:1.english: One mentions the might of the rains - [Namely,] "He makes the wind blow [and the rain to fall]," as this is not an expression of request, but rather an expression of mention and praise.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:11:2.hebrew: ושואלין - ותן טל ומטר, לשון בקשה:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:11:2.english: And one asks - “And grant dew and rain,” [which is] an expression of request.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:11:3.hebrew: והבדלה בחונן הדעת - במוצאי שבת: "אתה חוננתנו":
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:11:3.english: And Havdalah in [the blessing of] "Who graciously grants knowledge" - On Saturday night: [reciting] "You have graciously endowed us" [Attah Chonantanu].

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:17:1.hebrew: מתוך שהיא חכמה - החכם יודע להבדיל בין קדש לחול, ובין טמא לטהור:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:17:1.english: Because it is wisdom - A wise person knows how to distinguish between the sacred and the profane, and between the impure and the pure.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:19:1.hebrew: בין שתי אותיות - בין שתי הזכרות:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:19:1.english: Between two letters - Between two mentions [of God's Name].

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:1.hebrew: במילתה מיהא גדולה היא - במקום שצריכה נקמה, דבר גדול הוא:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:1.english: At least in its [own] context it is great - In a place where vengeance is needed, it is a great thing.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:2.hebrew: שתי נקמות הללו למה - אחת לרעה, להנקם מן העכו"ם שלא קבלו את התורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:2.english: Why [are] these two vengeances [mentioned]? - One [is] for evil, to take vengeance upon the idolaters who did not accept the Torah.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:3.hebrew: ואחת לטובה - כדאמרינן בב"ק (דף לח.): מפארן הופיע, והפקיר ממונן לישראל — שור של ישראל שנגח שור של עכו"ם, פטור:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:3.english: And one for good - As we say in Bava Kamma (38a): From Paran He shined forth, and He made their property ownerless to Israel — [for example,] an ox of an Israelite that gored an ox of an idolater is exempt.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:4.hebrew: הופיע - גלה והפקיר כשלא קבלו את התורה:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:23:4.english: He shined forth - He exposed [their property] and declared [it] ownerless when they did not accept the Torah.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:26:1.hebrew: בתחלה - כשעלו מן הגולה והיו דחוקים:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:26:1.english: Initially - When they came up from the Exile and were in straitened circumstances.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:26:2.english: They became wealthy - [Enough] to buy wine.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:26:3.hebrew: קבעוה על הכוס - ואז נשתכח תקנת עזרא, וכשחזרו והענו, קבעוה בתפלה, ונחלקו היאך יאמרוה:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:26:3.english: They established it over the cup - And then the enactment of Ezra was forgotten, and when they became impoverished again, they established it in the prayer, and they disagreed over how they should recite it.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:29:1.hebrew: מפני שיכול - משמע: אם ירצה שלא לחזור ולהתפלל. הא אם אמרה בתפלה — א"צ לאומרה על הכוס:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:29:1.english: Because he is able - This implies [that he may do so] if he wishes not to return and pray [again]. But if he recited it in prayer, he does not need to recite it over the cup.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:31:1.english: And I heard - [This means:] I heard.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:37:1.english: Returns to the beginning - [Both] for the prayer and for the cup.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:3:1.hebrew: אבל עקרב פוסק - ונוטלו, לפי שהעקרב מסוכן לעקוץ יותר משנחש מוכן לישוך:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:3:1.english: But [for] a scorpion he stops - And removes it, because a scorpion is more liable to sting than a snake is prone to bite.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:4:1.hebrew: אין מעידין עליו - לומר לאשתו: "מת בעליך", להתירה לינשא — פעמים שאין האריות רעבים, ואין אוכלין אותו:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:4:1.english: They do not testify about him - To say to his wife, "Your husband has died," to permit her to remarry — [for] at times the lions are not hungry, and they do not eat him.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:4:2.hebrew: נחשים ועקרבים - או זה או זה, מעידים עליו שמת. אלמא, מועד הנחש לישוך:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:4:2.english: Snakes and scorpions - [Whether it was] either this or that, they testify about him that he died. Evidently, a snake is prone to bite.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:5:1.hebrew: אגב איצצא - כשנפל עליהם ודחקם, הזיקוהו:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:5:1.english: Due to the pressure - When he fell upon them and pressed them, they harmed him.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:6:1.english: An innocuous ox - That has not gored a person.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:6:2.english: Forewarned - [An ox] that has gored three times.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:7:1.hebrew: בדקולא - סל שתולין בו תבן בראשו, ואוכל:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:7:1.english: In the basket - A basket containing straw that they hang on its head, and it eats.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:7:2.hebrew: ושדי דרגא - לאו דוקא, אלא כלומר: הזהר ממנו הרבה:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:7:2.english: And throw down the ladder - Not literally, but rather, that is to say: Be very cautious of it.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:7:3.hebrew: ביומי ניסן - מתוך שעברו ימי הסתיו שהארץ יבשה, ועכשיו רואה אותה מלאה דשאים — זחה דעתו עליו, ונכנס בו יצר הרע:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:7:3.english: During the days of Nisan - Since the days of winter have passed, when the earth was dry, and now he sees it full of grass, his mind becomes haughty, and an evil urge enters into him.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:8:1.hebrew: ערוד - מן הנחש והצב בא, שנזקקין זה עם זה, ויוצא משניהם ערוד:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:8:1.english: An arvad - It comes from the snake and the lizard, for they mate with one another, and an arvad emerges from both of them.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:8:2.english: Its hole - From which it emerges.

Rashi on Berakhot 33a:8:3.hebrew: ומת הערוד - מצאתי בה"ג: אמרי במערבא, כשהערוד נושך את האדם, אם הערוד קודם למים — מת האדם, ואם האדם קודם למים — מת הערוד. ונעשה נס לר' חנינא, ונקבע מעין מתחת עקבו:
Rashi on Berakhot 33a:8:3.english: And the arvad died - I found in Halakhot Gedolot: They say in the West [the Land of Israel]: When an arvad bites a person, if the arvad reaches water first, the person dies; and if the person reaches water first, the arvad dies. And a miracle occurred for Rabbi Ḥanina, and a spring was established beneath his heel.

Tosafot on Berakhot 33a:3:1.hebrew: אבל עקרב פוסק - בירושלמי קאמר דאם היה נחש מרתיע לבא כנגדו — פוסק, לפי שבא כנגדו בכעס, מתכוין להזיקו. ומיהו לא מצינו אם פסק שיחזור לראש, מדלא קאמר: "ואם פסק חוזר לראש"; אבל לתחלת ברכה מיהא יחזור. ואם טעה בג' ראשונות או בג' אחרונות — חוזר לתחלת הג': באבות בראשונות, ובעבודה באחרונות, כדאמרינן לקמן בפרקין (ברכות דף לד.):
Tosafot on Berakhot 33a:3:1.english: "But [for] a scorpion, he stops" - In the Yerushalmi it says that if a snake was darting forward to come toward him, he stops, because it comes toward him in anger, intending to harm him. However, we have not found that if he stopped, he must return to the beginning [of the prayer], since [the Gemara] does not state, "And if he stopped, he returns to the beginning"; but he must at least return to the beginning of the blessing. And if he erred in the first three or in the last three [blessings], he returns to the beginning of the three: to Avot for the first [three], and to Avodah for the last [three], as we say later in our chapter (Berakhot 34a).
